sentences.text: 4. Undisputed fact is that the offending Jeep bearing registration number MP04-T-6105 was insured by the Insurance Company.

5. According to the claimants, on 27/06/2010 at about 15:15 hours, offending Jeep bearing registration number MP04-T-6105 dashed the Motorcycle of deceased Yogendra Singh, as a result,
he fell down and sustained injuries on his head, leg and different parts of body.
It is alleged that driver of the Jeep was driving the Jeep in a rash and negligent manner.
Yogendra Singh lost his life on 03/07/2010 in Sahara Hospital, Gwalior during his treatment.
After merg enquiry, police registered Crime No. 411/2010 against the driver of offending Jeep/respondent No. 1 for offences under Sections 279, 337 and 304A of IPC.
6. Claimants who are mother, father and minor sister of deceased preferred claim petition on the ground that deceased was aged about 23 years.

He was working as a Constable in CISF and was earning Rs. 18,000 per month by way of salary and, accordingly, the claimants have been deprived of the part of salary which deceased would have spent on the claimants.
Accordingly, they preferred claim petition for recovery of compensation amount of Rs. 91,42,000/-.
7. Respondent No. 1/owner and driver of the offending vehicle filed the written statement and denied the accident.

However it was admitted by respondent No. 1 that he is the driver of Jeep bearing registration number MP04- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10199 T-6105 which was insured with respondent No. 2/Company.
It was claimed that a false claim petition has been filed in order to claim compensation.
8. The Insurance Company filed its written statement and denied the accident.
A vague reply was given that in absence of confirmed insurance policy, insurance of offending vehicle with Insurance Company is denied.

In the alternative, it was pleaded that if it is found that the offending vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company then the claim petition is liable to be dismissed on the ground that the information about the accident was given by hospital to police after 8 days of the accident and statement was recorded by police after 01 month and 15 days of the accident with regard to Smt.Siya Devi vs Vijay Sharma on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100321065/
2
involvement of Jeep in question.
Thus, the Insurance Company also denied the factum of accident.

9. The claimants in support of their claim examined Sunil Kumar Verma (PW-1) to prove the salary slip of deceased, Smt. Siyadevi (PW-2), mother of deceased, Narendra Singh (PW-3) who claimed to be the eye-witness, Sughar Singh (PW-4), father of deceased and Gyan Singh (PW-5) who was also eye- witness.

Neither the Insurance Company/appellant nor the owner or driver of the offending Jeep entered in the witness box and they also did not examine any other witness in their support.
10.
The trial Court after framing issues and recording evidence of the witnesses allowed the claim and awarded Rs.15,90,000/- to the appellants.

11. Challenging the liability of Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount it is submitted by counsel for appellant that in MLC (Ex.P/12) it was mentioned - "H/o:- RTA eksVjlkbfdy ls ,DlhMsaV ".

It is submitted that therefore it is clear that in the information given to doctor for the first time, it was alleged that deceased had met with a Motorcycle accident, whereas in the present case offending vehicle is a Jeep.

It is further submitted that the accident took place on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10199 27/06/2010, whereas FIR was lodged on 12/08/2010 and,
thus, it is clear that the offending Jeep was falsely implicated in order to lodge a false claim case.
12. Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by counsel for the claimants.

13. So far as pre-MLC (Ex. P/12) is concerned, it is mentioned that eksVjlkbfdy ls ,DlhMsaV. The deceased was undisputedly going on a motorcycle and the case of claimants is that offending Jeep had dashed the Motorcycle.

Therefore if the informant had informed the doctor that deceased had suffered injuries in an accident by motorcycle, then it cannot be presumed that in fact the deceased was dashed by Motorcycle and not by a Jeep.

So far as delayed lodging of FIR is concerned, it is suffice to mention here that the deceased lost his life in Sahara Hospital on 03/07/2010 while he was under medical treatment and merg intimation (Ex.P/6) was given to SHO Police Station Jhansi Road, Gwalior from where the information was forwarded to Police Station Civil Lines, Morena and merg enquiry was conducted by the police and on the basis of statements of witnesses the FIR was lodged.

If the police was lethargic in conducting the merg enquiry and completed the same belatedly, then on account of lethargic attitude of police, it cannot be said that the offending vehicle was falsely implicated at a later stage.
Furthermore it is well established principle of law that claim petitions are to be decided on the basis of evidence led before the Claims Tribunal.

Even otherwise,
FIR is not a substantive piece of evidence.

Furthermore where a boy aged about 23 years was fighting for his life and family members were busy in his treatment, then it was not expected from them that instead of getting their child treated they should have rushed to the police station to lodge the FIR.
Furthermore, neither the owner/driver of the offending vehicle nor the Insurance Company dared to enter in the witness box and no evidence was led by the respondents.

sentences.text:
Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by holding that Insurance Company is jointly and severally responsible to pay the compensation amount.
15.

Although, it was submitted by counsel for Insurance Company that excessive compensation has been awarded, but since claimants have also filed M.A. No.1149 of 2014, therefore, the submission of counsel for Insurance Company with regard to quantum of compensation, shall be considered in M.A. No.1149/2014, in order to avoid repetition.
16.
Accordingly M.A. No. 1159 of 2014 is, hereby, dismissed.
M.A. Number 1149 of 2014 17.

Challenging the sufficiency of compensation amount, it is submitted by counsel for appellants that according to the salary slip of deceased (Ex.P/1), it is clear that on the date of his death, his take home salary was Rs.15012/- and the Claims Tribunal has wrongly deducted Rs.1453/- towards standard deductions.
In fact, the Claims Tribunal should have taken the entire take home salary for the purpose of calculating loss of income.
It is further submitted that future prospects have not been awarded and less amount has been paid under the head of consortium.
18. Per contra, counsel for Insurance Company submitted that the Claims Tribunal has wrongly assessed the take home salary of deceased.

19. Heard, learned counsel for the parties.
20.
The claimants have relied upon Pay Certificate (Ex.P/1), according to which, the take-home salary of deceased in the month of July 2010 would have been rupees Rs.15012/-.
Since deceased had died on 3/7/2010 therefore Rs. 1453/-
were drawn towards salary from 1/7/2010 to 3/7/2010 and deductions to the tune of Rs. 277/- were also made.
The Claims Tribunal has deducted Rs.1453/- towards standard deductions.

It appears that the Claims Tribunal committed an error by deducting Rs.1453/- towards standard deductions because NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10199 as per Pay Certificate (Ex.P/1), Rs.1453/- were drawn towards salary of deceased from 1/7/2010 to 3/7/2010 and the amount of Rs.1453/- was not towards standard deductions.
From the Pay Certificate (Ex. P/1), it is clear that Rs.30/- were deducted towards CGEGIS, Rs. 122/- were deducted towards GPF/Tier-I, Rs.125/- were deducted towards CGHS.
In all Rs.277/- were deducted.

From the pay certificate, it is clear that out of total salary of Rs.15012/-,
Rs.6720/- was by way of basic pay, Rs.2000/- by way of GP, Rs.3924/- by way of DA., Rs. 60/- were added by way of W/A, Rs.870 were added by way of TPT and Rs.1438 by way of COR.
It is fairly conceded by counsel for claimants that COR means cost of ration, TPT means transportation allowance and W/A is washing allowance.
These allowances are payable to the employee therefore these allowances cannot be added in the take home salary of deceased.
Thus, it is clear that out of gross monthly salary of Rs.15012/-, an amount of Rs.2368/- was liable to be deducted and take home salary of deceased has to be taken as Rs.12644/-.
Thus it is clarified that for the purposes of loss of dependency, the income of deceased would be treated as Rs.12644/- per month.

The other terms and conditions of the award shall remain the same.

22. With aforesaid modification, the Award dated 11/09/2014 passed by IV Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 356 of 2013 passed by the Claims Tribunal is hereby affirmed.
